subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Pelvic Types: Gynaecoid, Android, Anthropoid and Platypelloid

steps.tx: The round, roomy female pelvis ideal for childbirth is the **gynaecoid pelvis**. All diameters are adequate and the subpubic angle is wide. About half of women have predominantly this pelvic shape. Its brim index and wide sciatic notch let the head rotate in the roomy posterior segment.
steps.say: The gynaecoid pelvis is round and roomy, ideal for childbirth in about half of women.

steps.tx: The heart shaped, narrow pelvis resembling the male form is the **android pelvis**. Its funnel shape arrests descent in the midpelvis and deep transverse arrest is characteristic. Operative delivery rates rise with this type. The heart shaped brim pushes the head occipitoposterior, and narrow pubic arch steals outlet room.
steps.say: The android pelvis funnels narrowly and characteristically arrests descent in the midpelvis.

steps.tx: The long anteroposterior oval pelvis favouring occipitoposterior positions is the **anthropoid pelvis**. Its roomy back segment accommodates the occiput posteriorly. Face to pubes delivery may occur spontaneously in this type. Deep transverse arrest is rare here; persistent occipitoposterior positions deliver face to pubes in a third of cases.
steps.say: The anthropoid pelvis favours occipitoposterior positions with its roomy back segment.

steps.tx: The flat pelvis with shortened front to back diameter is the **platypelloid pelvis**. Engagement happens in the transverse diameter with marked lateral tilt of the head. It is the least common of the four pure types. The head enters with exaggerated asynclitism, the parietal bone presenting first, until the brim is negotiated.
steps.say: The platypelloid pelvis is flat front to back and engages the head transversely.

steps.tx: Among the four pure shapes in the Caldwell Moloy classification, the flat **platypelloid pelvis** is the least common. Its front to back diameter is shortened, so the fetal head engages in the transverse diameter with a marked lateral tilt. Engagement uses exaggerated asynclitism, and the parietal bone presents first until the brim is negotiated. The name states how the head must enter, not merely that the brim looks wide from side to side.
steps.say: The platypelloid pelvis is the uncommon flat brim in the four type classification. A short front to back diameter forces the head to engage transversely, with lateral tilt and exaggerated asynclitism, the parietal bone leading until the brim is passed.

vis.caption: Gynaecoid, android, anthropoid, and platypelloid brims are set side by side as the four pure pelvic types. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The classification grouping pelves by brim shape is the **Caldwell-Moloy classification**. Most real pelves mix features of two types, such as gynaecoid with android tendencies. Clinical pelvimetry and labour progress matter more than labels. Most pelves are mixed, so the type is named by the posterior segment, which governs rotation.
steps.say: Caldwell-Moloy classifies brim shapes, though most real pelves mix two types.

steps.tx: The clinical estimate of the true conjugate taken vaginally is the **diagonal conjugate**. Measured from sacral promontory to lower pubic border, about twelve and a half centimetres is normal. Subtracting one and a half to two gives the obstetric conjugate. Twelve and a half centimetres minus one and a half to two gives the 10.5 to 11 centimetre obstetric conjugate.
steps.say: The diagonal conjugate estimates the true conjugate by subtracting about two centimetres.

steps.tx: Pelvic adequacy is judged in labour by progress, the philosophy of **trial of labour**. Imaging pelvimetry rarely predicts outcome accurately outside extreme contraction. A well conducted trial with monitoring is the best test of the pelvis. Caesarean for suspected disproportion without a trial in labour overdiagnoses pelvic contraction in most series.
steps.say: Trial of labour tests pelvic adequacy better than imaging pelvimetry in most cases.

steps.tx: Short stature, rickets and pelvic injury history flag possible **contracted pelvis**. Clinical assessment of conjugates, spines and outlet follows. Known severe contraction plans caesarean delivery before labour. A height under 145 centimetres prompts pelvic assessment, though most short women still deliver vaginally.
steps.say: Contracted pelvis is flagged by short stature, rickets or pelvic injury history.

steps.tx: The widest transverse diameter of the brim and the interspinous of the midpelvis each limit descent at their level, together called **transverse diameters**. Midpelvic contraction matters more because it cannot be bypassed by head moulding alone. The interspinous diameter near 10.5 centimetres is the narrowest the head meets after engagement.
steps.say: Transverse diameters limit descent at brim and midpelvis, with midpelvic contraction mattering most.
